config.title: Platform Detection Widget

intro.title: Platform Detection Widget
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple widget that detects and displays the current platform your app is running on, such as iOS, Android, or the web. You'll learn how to use the Capacitor Platform API to access device information in a cross-platform way. The main technologies involved are Ionic for the UI, Angular for the component structure, and Capacitor for native platform detection. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to working with platform-specific features in a hybrid mobile app.
intro.usecase: Platform detection is essential in cross-platform mobile apps to deliver tailored experiences for iOS, Android, and web users. Real-world examples include apps like Spotify adjusting player controls for iOS gestures, banking apps showing biometric login options based on platform capabilities, and e-commerce apps optimizing checkout flows for mobile versus desktop. Developers use platform detection to conditionally load native plugins, apply platform-specific UI styling, or enable hardware features like camera or GPS that behave differently across devices. This pattern appears in settings panels that show device-specific options, onboarding flows that adapt to platform conventions, and analytics dashboards that track usage by operating system.

objectives: Import the Platform service from @ionic/angular to access device detection capabilities.
Apply dependency injection to inject the Platform service into a component's constructor.
Utilize the Platform service's is() method to check for specific platforms like 'ios' or 'android'.
Implement boolean properties in the component class to store platform detection results.
Execute conditional logic in the component's ngOnInit() lifecycle hook to initialize platform detection.
Construct template expressions using Angular interpolation to display platform-specific text.
Use the *ngIf structural directive to conditionally render UI elements based on platform detection.
Apply CSS classes dynamically with [class] binding to style elements differently per platform.
Implement a method to return platform-specific configuration values based on detection results.
Handle platform detection changes by subscribing to the Platform service's ready() observable.
Define a component interface with properties for platform-specific data storage.
Access Capacitor's getPlatform() utility to retrieve the current native platform when applicable.

steps.title: Import Ionic Angular core components
steps.instruction: Import the following Ionic UI components from '@ionic/angular': IonCard, IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle, IonCardContent, IonList, IonItem, IonLabel, IonIcon, and IonBadge.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple named exports from '@ionic/angular'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing Ionic components
import { IonButton, IonContent, IonHeader } from '@ionic/angular';

seedCode.App.tsx: // Import Ionic Angular core components here

steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for Ionic UI components is added to the file.
successCriteria: The code includes a valid import statement from '@ionic/angular' with IonCard, IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle, IonCardContent, IonList, IonItem, IonLabel, IonIcon, and IonBadge.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Ionic UI components needed for building the widget interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some Ionic components, but not all required ones. Make sure to include IonCard, IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle, IonCardContent, IonList, IonItem, IonLabel, IonIcon, and IonBadge.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import IonCard, IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle, IonCardContent, IonList, IonItem, IonLabel, IonIcon, and IonBadge from '@ionic/angular'.

steps.title: Import Capacitor platform detection utilities
steps.instruction: Import Capacitor from '@capacitor/core' and Platform from '@ionic/angular'.
steps.hint: Add two import statements at the top of your file: one for Capacitor and one for Platform.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have imported the Capacitor core API and Ionic's Platform service, which are needed for platform detection.
successCriteria: The code must include two import statements: one importing Capacitor from '@capacitor/core' and one importing Platform from '@ionic/angular'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported both Capacitor and Platform. These will allow you to detect the current platform in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but you need to import both Capacitor from '@capacitor/core' and Platform from '@ionic/angular'. Check that both import statements are present.
steps.feedbackWrong: This step requires importing Capacitor from '@capacitor/core' and Platform from '@ionic/angular'. Make sure you add both import statements at the top of your file.

steps.title: Create the PlatformDetectionComponent class
steps.instruction: Create the PlatformDetectionComponent class with the @Component decorator. Set the selector to 'app-platform-detection' and standalone to true.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define your component class.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a PlatformDetectionComponent class defined with the @Component decorator configured with selector and standalone properties.
successCriteria: The code must include a class named PlatformDetectionComponent decorated with @Component, with selector set to 'app-platform-detection' and standalone set to true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the PlatformDetectionComponent class with the correct @Component decorator configuration.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you have: 1) The class name PlatformDetectionComponent, 2) The @Component decorator, 3) selector: 'app-platform-detection', 4) standalone: true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class wasn't created correctly. Make sure to use the @Component decorator with the specified selector and standalone properties.

steps.title: Add component imports and template
steps.instruction: Add the imports array to the @Component decorator with Ionic UI components (IonCard, IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle, IonCardContent) and define a template with an empty IonCard element.
steps.hint: The imports array goes inside the @Component decorator. The template should contain a single IonCard element with no content yet.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have the necessary Ionic UI components imported and a basic template structure with an IonCard.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator should include an imports array with IonCard, IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle, and IonCardContent, and a template property with an empty <ion-card> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the Ionic component imports and defined the template structure with an IonCard.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added all four Ionic components to the imports array and included the template property with an empty <ion-card> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component is missing either the imports array with Ionic components or the template property with an IonCard element. Check the @Component decorator configuration.

steps.title: Define platform detection properties
steps.instruction: Inside the PlatformDetectionComponent class, add four properties: isWeb (boolean), isIOS (boolean), isAndroid (boolean), and platformName (string). Initialize them with default values.
steps.hint: Add properties directly in the class body. Use TypeScript type annotations to specify their types.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class now has typed properties to store platform detection results.
successCriteria: The PlatformDetectionComponent class contains four typed properties: isWeb (boolean), isIOS (boolean), isAndroid (boolean), and platformName (string). All properties should have default values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the platform detection properties with proper TypeScript types and default values.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some properties, but check that you have all four: isWeb (boolean), isIOS (boolean), isAndroid (boolean), and platformName (string). Make sure each has a type annotation and a default value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class doesn't contain the required platform detection properties. Add isWeb, isIOS, isAndroid (all booleans) and platformName (string) with default values inside the class body.

steps.title: Implement platform detection method
steps.instruction: Add a detectPlatform() method to the PlatformDetectionComponent class that uses Capacitor's getPlatform() and Platform.is() to set the component's platform detection properties.
steps.hint: Create a method named detectPlatform() that checks the current platform and assigns boolean values to the properties you defined earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a detectPlatform() method that can determine the current platform and update the component's properties accordingly.
successCriteria: The PlatformDetectionComponent class should contain a detectPlatform() method that sets the isWeb, isIOS, and isAndroid properties based on Capacitor platform detection.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the platform detection method. The detectPlatform() method will allow your component to identify which platform it's running on.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your detectPlatform() method properly sets all three platform properties (isWeb, isIOS, isAndroid) using Capacitor's platform detection.
steps.feedbackWrong: The detectPlatform() method is missing or doesn't properly set the platform properties. Remember to use Capacitor.getPlatform() or Platform.is() to detect the current platform and assign the correct boolean values to the component's properties.

steps.title: Initialize platform detection on component creation
steps.instruction: Add the ngOnInit lifecycle hook to your component and call the detectPlatform() method inside it.
steps.hint: Implement the OnInit interface and add ngOnInit() method to run platform detection when the component initializes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will implement the OnInit interface and call detectPlatform() when it initializes.
successCriteria: Component implements OnInit interface, has ngOnInit() method, and calls detectPlatform() inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the ngOnInit lifecycle hook and called the platform detection method. This ensures platform detection runs automatically when the component is created.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've implemented the OnInit interface, added the ngOnInit() method, and called detectPlatform() inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have the ngOnInit lifecycle hook implemented correctly. Remember to implement OnInit interface and call detectPlatform() inside ngOnInit().

steps.title: Add card header with title
steps.instruction: Inside the component's template, add an IonCardHeader with an IonCardTitle that displays the text 'Platform Detection'.
steps.hint: Use the Ionic card components to create a header section with a title. The template should contain <ion-card-header> and <ion-card-title> elements.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding a card header with title
<ion-card>
  <ion-card-header>
    <ion-card-title>My Component Title</ion-card-title>
  </ion-card-header>
</ion-card>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now includes a card header section with a title 'Platform Detection' using Ionic components.
successCriteria: The template should contain an <ion-card-header> element with an <ion-card-title> child element displaying 'Platform Detection'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the card header with the title 'Platform Detection'. This creates a clear visual section for your platform detection widget.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the <ion-card-header> and <ion-card-title> elements with the correct text content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required card header structure. Please add an <ion-card-header> with an <ion-card-title> displaying 'Platform Detection'.

steps.title: Create platform status list
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add an IonCardContent element containing an IonList with three IonItem elements to display platform statuses.
steps.hint: Use the Ionic components to structure the list. Each IonItem will later show a platform name and its detection status.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding a list structure in Ionic Angular
<IonCardContent>
  <IonList>
    <IonItem>
      <IonLabel>Item 1</IonLabel>
    </IonItem>
    <IonItem>
      <IonLabel>Item 2</IonLabel>
    </IonItem>
    <IonItem>
      <IonLabel>Item 3</IonLabel>
    </IonItem>
  </IonList>
</IonCardContent>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a structured list inside a card content area, ready to display platform detection results.
successCriteria: The template includes IonCardContent wrapping an IonList with exactly three IonItem elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the list structure to display platform statuses.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have IonCardContent containing IonList with three IonItem elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The list structure isn't correct. Check that you have IonCardContent > IonList > three IonItem elements in the template.

steps.title: Add platform status badges
steps.instruction: Inside each IonItem in your template, add an IonBadge element that displays 'Detected' or 'Not Detected' based on the corresponding boolean property (isWeb, isIOS, isAndroid).
steps.hint: Use *ngIf on the IonBadge to conditionally show 'Detected' when the property is true, and 'Not Detected' when false. Remember to import CommonModule in your component's imports array if you haven't already.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of conditional badge inside an IonItem -->
<IonItem>
  <IonLabel>Web</IonLabel>
  <IonBadge *ngIf="isWeb">Detected</IonBadge>
  <IonBadge *ngIf="!isWeb">Not Detected</IonBadge>
</IonItem>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will include IonBadge elements inside each IonItem that visually indicate whether each platform is detected.
successCriteria: The template contains IonBadge elements with *ngIf conditions checking isWeb, isIOS, and isAndroid properties, displaying appropriate 'Detected'/'Not Detected' text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional badges to show platform detection status. This provides clear visual feedback to users.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure each IonItem has both badges (one for 'Detected' when true, one for 'Not Detected' when false) using *ngIf conditions.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added IonBadge elements inside each IonItem with *ngIf conditions based on the boolean properties. The badges should show 'Detected' or 'Not Detected' text.

steps.title: Display detected platform name
steps.instruction: Add a final IonItem below the existing list in your template that displays 'Current Platform:' followed by the actual platform name detected by Capacitor. Use the Platform enum from Capacitor to get the platform name string.
steps.hint: Add an IonItem with IonLabel inside your template. Use the Platform enum (e.g., Platform.Web) to display the platform name as a string.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of displaying platform name in template
<ion-item>
  <ion-label>Current Platform: {{ platformName }}</ion-label>
</ion-item>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will include a final IonItem that shows the current platform name detected by Capacitor.
successCriteria: Uses Platform enum to show platform name
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added the platform name display. The final IonItem will show users exactly which platform their app is running on.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the Platform enum from Capacitor to get the platform name string, and that the IonItem is placed below the existing list in your template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The platform name display wasn't added correctly. Remember to add an IonItem with IonLabel that shows 'Current Platform:' followed by the actual platform name from Capacitor's Platform enum.

steps.title: Style the component with Ionic utilities
steps.instruction: Add Ionic CSS utility classes to your component: add `class='ion-padding'` to the IonCard element, and add appropriate color classes to the IonBadge elements (use `color='success'` for detected platforms and `color='medium'` for not detected platforms).
steps.hint: IonCard should have class='ion-padding'. For IonBadge, use color='success' when the platform is detected (true) and color='medium' when not detected (false).
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of Ionic utility classes -->
<IonCard class="ion-padding">
  <IonBadge color="success">Active</IonBadge>
  <IonBadge color="medium">Inactive</IonBadge>
</IonCard>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have visual polish with proper padding on the card and color-coded badges that clearly indicate which platforms are detected.
successCriteria: IonCard has class='ion-padding'. Each IonBadge has color='success' when its corresponding platform property is true, and color='medium' when false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added Ionic's CSS utility classes for visual polish. The card now has proper padding and the badges are color-coded to clearly show which platforms are detected.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but check: 1) Does the IonCard have class='ion-padding'? 2) Do all three IonBadge elements have the correct color classes (success for detected, medium for not detected)?
steps.feedbackWrong: The styling isn't quite right. Remember to add class='ion-padding' to the IonCard, and use color='success' for detected platforms and color='medium' for not detected platforms on the IonBadge elements.
